name: runtime-strings
description: Real-world version strings for Penthera's runtime-advisory check, labelled by hand from primary sources. See docs/research/runtime-strings.md.
license: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Individual strings are factual version identifiers quoted from the cited sources.

verdict_words.affected: exact upstream version below the fix
verdict_words.end-of-life-no-fix: the version is on an end-of-life line the advisory gives no fix for
verdict_words.check-on-server: the product is in use but the string cannot say (hidden, partial, floating, distribution build)
verdict_words.has-fix: at or above the fixed version (as advertised)
verdict_words.none: not in the advisory's scope, or no evidence (omitted from `verdicts`)

categories.exact-upstream: An exact upstream version as the product prints it
categories.distro-backport: A distribution build that says so (a package revision, or a Server header naming the distribution)
categories.distro-unmarked: A distribution build whose string is identical to an upstream one
categories.hidden-partial: The product with its version hidden or cut short (ServerTokens, server_tokens, expose_php, PHPSESSID, composer.json)
categories.docker-pinned: Official Docker image tags with an exact version
categories.docker-floating: Official Docker image tags that float (8.3, fpm, latest, lts, stable)
categories.end-of-life: Exact or line-only versions on release lines past their end of support
categories.lookalike: Strings and images that look like one of the products but are not

B1.title: `introduced` is ignored for release lines older than the one the flaw was introduced on
B1.detail: CVE-2021-41773/42013 exist only in httpd 2.4.49 and 2.4.50 (`introduced: 2.4.49` on the 2.4 line). An exact 2.2 or 2.0 version is reported as "end of life, no fix" (critical, potential) for it, a distribution 2.2 build and a line-only 2.2 tag as "check on server". Lines below the oldest line that carries `introduced` cannot have the flaw.
B1.fix: In verdictFor, when the version's line has no fix entry and is older than the oldest listed line, and that line's entry has `introduced`, return none.

B2.title: Pre-release versions are misread: -dev as a distribution build, RC/beta as no version
B2.detail: PHP/8.4.27-dev (a PHP-8.4 branch build from before 8.4.27) is reported as "has the fix": the -dev suffix is taken for a distribution build string and its upstream number compared with the fix. PHP/8.5.0RC1 and php:8.5.0RC1 parse as no version ("check on server" instead of affected); PHP/8.6.0RC4 gets "check on server" for advisories that do not cover 8.6. Python's 3.15.0rc1 and OpenSSL's 4.1.0-beta2 are dropped or taken for distribution builds.
B2.fix: Parse -dev, alpha, beta and RC (any case, with or without a separator) as a pre-release of the upstream number, sorting below the release, and never as a distribution build.

B3.title: Python banners with only major.minor are ignored
B3.detail: aiohttp sends Server: Python/3.9 aiohttp/3.8.6 (aiohttp/http.py). The Python banner pattern needs x.y.z, so an end-of-life 3.9 is not reported; PHP's pattern already accepts x.y.
B3.fix: Accept Python/x.y in the banner pattern, which gives `branch` evidence.

B4.title: Node.js LTS codenames are not resolved to their line
B4.detail: nvm accepts lts/iron in .nvmrc and the node image has iron, jod and hydrogen tags. They read as no version, so lts/iron (Node.js 20, end of life 30 Apr 2026) is not reported as end of life.
B4.fix: Map the LTS codenames (argon 4 … krypton 24) to their major line in lib/advisories/products.js.

L1.title: A distribution build whose string equals an upstream one is read as upstream
L1.detail: Debian 11-13 and Ubuntu 24.04+ print plain upstream PHP numbers (PHP/8.3.6), RHEL never adds a suffix, Debian's and RHEL's nginx add no OS token, and distribution Pythons print sys.version. Without a Server header naming the distribution, these read as exact upstream builds: PHP/8.3.6 from a patched Ubuntu 24.04 is reported critical and likely affected. The promise holds only for strings that mark themselves as distribution builds.
L1.fix: Not fixable from the string alone. Decided by the maintainer: such a banner gives at most `potential`, with a check-on-server note (#114). The verdict stays "affected" (labels here are verdicts, not confidence), so these entries keep this deviation. A list of frozen distribution versions in the pack is a possible follow-up.

G1.title: Only official library images are read
G1.detail: nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27 is nginx 1.27 (end of life) and mongodb/mongodb-community-server:7.0-ubi8 is MongoDB 7.0, but neither is a library/ image, so there is no evidence. Absence is not reported as safe, so no promise breaks.
G1.fix: Optionally add well-known vendor images (nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged, bitnami/*) to dockerImages.
